choose-coordinate: Imagine sliding the bead without changing what it is made of. Which quantity changes?
Which symbol tells where to draw the bead, before you compute what is pushing on it?
constraint: If the bead stays on the same circular wire, what distance from the centre stays fixed?
Mark two different points on the wire. Must neither coordinate move between them?
lagrangian: Write out the definition of L before replacing V with T.
Compare the operation between T and V in energy with the operation in the Lagrangian.
action: Two trips can end at the same place after following different paths. Which trip values enter the time integral?
Would two objects with the same mass but different paths necessarily have the same L at each moment?
stationary-action: What is varied in stationary action, the speed of the object or the path in the calculation?
At the top of a smooth hill the first change in height can vanish. What does that tell you about the word “stationary”?
spring-motion: When the cart is to the positive side of rest, which way is the spring stretched?
Is the spring at its rest length at the stated position?
pendulum-speed: Can a pendulum swing clockwise as well as counterclockwise?
What does the sign on an angular rate tell you about the rod rather than its length?
pendulum-kinetic: A reversed velocity still has a size. Check which quantity is squared in kinetic energy.
Try squaring a negative angular rate. What happens to its minus sign?
pendulum-potential: Compare the bob’s height at the bottom with its height after a small lift.
Potential energy depends on a chosen reference height. Where was the reference placed?
lagrangian-partial: A held-fixed quantity can have many values. Is the partial derivative asking you to erase q̇?
In this partial derivative, position and velocity are treated as separate inputs. Which input do you vary?
pendulum-motion: Would increasing mass change which side of equilibrium gravity pulls toward?
Check whether mass appears on both sides of the ideal pendulum equation before scaling the acceleration.
generalized-momentum: Inspect the mass factor in the kinetic energy before differentiating with respect to angular velocity.
Compare the units of length change and angle change. Which coordinate is conjugate to this momentum?
cyclic-coordinate: Check separately for the coordinate and its time rate. Which absence defines a cyclic coordinate?
A constant momentum and a zero momentum are different conditions. Which is needed here?
time-symmetry: Signs of coordinates and explicit appearances of the clock time are different clues. Look for t in the rule.
Could a formula use the same rule at noon and at 1 even if its input q had moved?
central-angular-momentum: Imagine a skater pulling their arms inward. Which two factors in angular momentum would you track as the skater spins?
Conserving a quantity means keeping its value. Does that restrict the value to zero?
effective-potential: Which energy was already present before the angular motion was removed from the radial equation?
Write the effective potential as a sum. What happened to the original potential term?
phase-point: What does the second axis on the phase-space diagram measure?
On the same vertical line of a phase diagram, mark momentum pointing each way. Are those marks on the same point?
hamiltonian: Is momentum used with its sign or squared in this particular energy term?
Did the size of the momentum actually become zero when you reversed its direction?
hamilton-position: The lower part of the partial-derivative symbol tells which input you vary. Which one is left?
Does holding a variable fixed require its value to be zero?
hamilton-momentum: A displaced spring still pulls on the cart. What changes its momentum?
On the positive side of rest, which way would the spring pull a released cart?
poisson-bracket: Write the two products of derivatives and then swap f and g. Which product comes first now?
Try functions other than the basic coordinate pair. Is there a reason every bracket should have the same number?
equilibrium-position: Sketch a hilltop with a horizontal tangent. What happens after a small nudge?
Would shifting the potential graph vertically alter the restoring force nearby?
local-stability: Compare the shapes of q⁴ and −q⁴ very near zero. What do their slopes and curvatures there have in common?
Can a flat-topped hill and a flat-bottomed valley share the result of this curvature test?
small-oscillation-rate: Look at where the mass sits in the square root for the oscillation rate.
Try putting the same spring under a heavier load. Which input to the frequency rule changed?
same-direction-mode: Mark both endpoints of the middle spring before and after the carts move. What distance does it sense?
Would a spring of ordinary stiffness stretch if both ends move equally in the same direction?
opposite-direction-mode: Draw the ends of the middle spring during opposite cart motion. Does their separation stay fixed?
A stiffer middle spring gives what change in restoring pull for the same extension?
moving-constraint: Picture a bead on a rail being raised by a lift. Can a position rule follow the rail?
A constraint specifies positions. Which position in this setup is set by the support?
constraint-rate: Draw the bead’s height today and just later as the support rises. What slope do those two records share?
Does following the support demand one constant speed, or matching its speed at each instant?
moving-origin: Which marker was used as the zero for q? Could that zero roll past someone on the ground?
Would changing a cart’s mass change the speed of the marker you measure from?
accelerating-origin: Compare what a ground observer and an accelerating marker would record for the same cart.
Did moving the reference marker add or remove any material from the cart?
constraint-multiplier: What equation comes from varying the multiplier rather than varying the bead position?
The term multiplied by λ contains which rule about allowed positions?
constraint-force: Sketch forces on the body and ask what net force could produce upward acceleration.
Does an upward-moving support switch off the downward gravitational force?
constraint-power: Energy transfer depends on force and displacement. Which way does the contact point move?
Could the support lift the object while gravity is still present?
radial-energy: Is there any change to the mass in the radial energy balance?
Check which part of the energy equation is proportional to the radial speed squared. Can that part be negative?
radial-turning-point: The word radial names just one direction. What about motion around the centre?
Does a momentarily unchanging radius require a vanishing rate of turn?
circular-orbit-radius: If an object has a radial velocity at the proposed circular radius, where will it be an instant later?
A circular orbit itself turns about the origin. Does turning require zero angular momentum?
circular-orbit-stability: A zero quadratic term leaves the next terms unknown. Could the graph bend up farther away?
Sketch two flat points that curve in opposite ways beyond the centre. Would this test separate them?
radial-oscillation-rate: One rate describes motion around the centre. What restores a small radial displacement?
Compare two differently shaped potentials at the same mass. Must their restoring slopes agree?
kepler-orbit-shape: In the orbit formula, what value of e would remove the angle-dependent part of the radius?
Choose two angles in the formula. What condition would give the same radius for both?
orbit-energy-shape: What sign of energy describes a closed, bound orbit for this potential and reference?
For a circle, inspect its energy relative to a body at rest infinitely far away.
rigid-point-velocity: Mark two dots on a rigid wheel. Which travels a longer arc in one turn?
For points on the same rotating object, which geometry enters speed = angular speed × distance?
axis-inertia: Check the exponent on distance in one mass’s inertia contribution.
The mass stays the same. Is the length of the lever arm also fixed?
inertia-tensor: Try a diagonal inertia table with different positive entries and a rotation along two axes. What happens to the component ratio?
A single vector direction is preserved by a matrix only for special directions. Which axes have that property here?
principal-axes: Changing coordinate axes does not remove material. What changes in the table that represents it?
The object can still be spinning in the new coordinates. Which couplings between different axes become simpler?
rigid-rotation-energy: Check whether the energy contains ω₂ or its square in these axes.
Replacing a component with its opposite does not add a second copy. Recalculate just its term.
euler-rigid-equation: An unchanged vector in space can have changing readings on turning axes. Which axes are being used?
A reference frame attached to the rotating body also turns. What links its three component equations?
intermediate-axis: Compare an exact spin with one given a tiny off-axis push. Which one is the stability test about?
Does growing away from one axis mean losing all rotational motion?
nonlinear-force: Write q³ as three q factors. How many of them double?
If the original q and coefficient are both nonzero, does doubling q remove that term?
phase-flow-arrow: Position alone does not set the momentum rate. What slope or force matters there?
Release a spring from rest away from equilibrium. What happens immediately after that zero-velocity instant?
pendulum-energy-contour: Which energy labels the original contour? Is it still the energy of the state later?
Does friction supply mechanical energy or take some away?
pendulum-energy-barrier: Is the energy high enough to pass the highest point, or only to turn back below it?
Check whether energy above the barrier can leave any kinetic energy at the top.
pendulum-separatrix: Near the upright position, does the small-angle period around the bottom still apply?
As the speed shrinks toward zero, what happens to the time required to cover each last part of the ascent?
driven-pendulum: Could a gentle repeating drive produce a matching repeating response?
Damping is one input. What do the observed motion and other parameters show?
poincare-sampling: Could an ordinary motion repeat on two alternating sample points?
Does sampling at the same drive phase answer the same question as sampling at random times?
sensitive-dependence: A deterministic rule can still amplify tiny differences. What does this short record establish?
A single unstable balance point can push nearby paths apart briefly. How would a longer test help?
canonical-pair: For a basic canonical pair, the coordinate and momentum scale factors must multiply to one. Test your factors.
If every old momentum were mapped to zero, could you recover the original state?
transformed-hamiltonian: Was the rule for any physical push changed, or only its coordinates?
Check whether the parameter representing the material in the cart was changed at all.
generating-function: Look for the rate of change of F₂ rather than its value. Which independent input is the old position?
There are two derivatives. The derivative with respect to new momentum gives which new variable?
time-dependent-canonical: Which part changes with time even if the old coordinates are held fixed?
Could a time-dependent adjustment to the energy rule let the usual Hamilton equations remain valid?
principal-action: Try substituting a candidate S into the equation for this particular system. What must cancel?
Is its value alone enough, or do its derivatives with respect to position and time enter?
hamilton-jacobi-equation: Which change in S turns an action into momentum dimensionally?
Compare the units of action divided by time with action divided by distance.
separate-action-time: Can a massive particle have an energy rule with no directly written t?
A potential can vary with position. Is that the same as containing t directly?
recover-hj-trajectory: Set the clock to the specified initial time in the solution and inspect the coordinate.
Check the units of Q in the free-cart position formula.
